sections.h2: Why does the county matter so much when selling a home in Florida?
sections.html:
Because the state is split into 67 counties and nearly every closing paper passes through one of their offices. Voters in each county pick a sheriff, tax collector, property appraiser, supervisor of elections and clerk of the circuit court for four year terms.

The rules come from Tallahassee, yet the people who apply them work down the street from the property. Two sellers in different counties follow the same statutes but may meet different hearing calendars, filing forms and local exemption votes. Treat the parcel's county as the starting point of every question.

This directory introduces the guides on Florida property tax, probate, foreclosure, eviction and selling. Use it to learn which office to call and which state page explains the rule behind the call.

Keep one folder per property with the deed, the latest tax bill, any exemption letter and the payoff statements. Those papers answer most questions a buyer, lender or title agent will ask.

sections.h2: Who handles what at the county level?
sections.html:
Four offices decide most of what a seller experiences.

  • The property appraiser sets value as of each January 1, mails the August proposed tax notice, and judges who gets an exemption.
  • The tax collector sends the bills in November, takes payments, sells tax certificates and handles deferral and installment requests.
  • The circuit court clerk records deeds, collects stamp tax with the recording, takes value board petitions, and runs foreclosure and tax deed auctions.
  • The sheriff serves eviction writs and, under section 82.036, clears people who occupy a home with no right to be there once an owner swears out a complaint.

The first three show up at nearly every sale, and a title company will order payoff and tax numbers from them. The calendar details come from the state revenue agency's taxpayer page.

sections.h2: What does the Florida property tax year look like?
sections.html:
It opens on January 1 with the value date and closes with an April 1 delinquency line. A handful of dates in between decide whether an owner keeps a benefit or loses a right to protest.

Dates in the Florida property tax year as listed on the state taxpayer page
DateEvent
January 1Value date for every parcel
March 1Last day to apply for exemptions or special classes
AugustProposed tax notice arrives by mail
25 days after that noticeWindow to file a value petition with the clerk
NovemberBills go out, and paying that month earns the biggest discount
April 1Taxes still open turn delinquent
By June 1Certificates sold on the unpaid items

The early payment discount drops a point each month after November.

sections.h2: Which homestead rules should a Florida seller know?
sections.html:
Section 196.031 builds the homestead exemption in two $25,000 layers. The lower layer reduces every levy, schools included, and the upper layer reduces only non school levies on value past the first $50,000. See the state revenue guide for the layout.

The form is DR-501, and the appraiser must have it by March 1. Living in the house as a permanent home on January 1 is a condition, and renting it out or moving away ends the benefit.

  • Save Our Homes caps yearly growth in taxable value at the lesser of 3 percent or inflation.
  • A sale resets the parcel to market based value the next January 1, except for items like spousal transfers.
  • Portability lets a saver carry the accumulated difference to a replacement home if the owner moves within the three year window.

sections.h2: What is the cost of moving title by deed?
sections.html:
The deed tax rate sits in section 201.02(1)(a). Seventy cents per $100 of price applies statewide with one exception, Miami-Dade.

That county charges 60 cents per $100 and adds a 45 cent surtax, which does not reach a deed that moves only a single family home. Price here is broad: cash, a released debt, and any loan on the property.

Recording a deed also carries per page clerk fees set in section 28.24, with a higher charge on page one. The clerk collects the stamp tax when the deed is recorded, so ask the county clerk for a full quote before closing.

sections.h2: How do estates, loans and tenants fit in?
sections.html:
Each topic has a state guide, and the county office named in it carries out the steps.

  • Probate: a smaller estate may use summary administration when non exempt assets stay at or under $150,000 or two years have passed since death (section 735.201). Florida collects no estate tax for deaths after the end of 2004.
  • Foreclosure: a court sale run by the clerk a few weeks after judgment, with the right to cure ending at the certificate of sale.
  • Eviction: short written notices, a sheriff writ and a 24 hour posting.
  • Tax sales: unpaid taxes turn into certificates, and a holder may seek a deed after two years.

Local dates and forms sit with the county, so use the county guides to find them.

sections.h2: What happens when property tax goes unpaid in Florida?
sections.html:
For each unpaid parcel the tax collector auctions a certificate, and the winner is whoever accepts the lowest interest rate. After two years the holder may ask for a tax deed.

Before any deed sale, the collector lists everyone who must be told: the titleholder, lienholders, mortgagees and contract for deed buyers, as section 197.502 lays out. The clerk runs the auction itself. On homestead land the opening bid also includes half of the latest assessed value.

Owners who are behind should phone the tax collector early. Installment prepayment and the homestead deferral both start in that office, and each has its own early deadline.

sections.h2: Which relief programs reach older owners and veterans?
sections.html:
Counties and cities may adopt extra relief, so the property appraiser is the place to learn what applies locally. The statutes set the outer limits.

  • Owners 65 or older may qualify for an added homestead break of up to $50,000 where a local ordinance allows it and household income fits the cap (section 196.075).
  • Veterans 65 or older with a permanent service connected disability may get a discount that matches the VA percentage (section 196.082).
  • A former servicemember with a disability rating of 10 percent or more may qualify for a $5,000 cut in assessed value.

Nothing here arrives on its own. File with the appraiser by March 1 and bring the paperwork the office requests.

sections.h2: How should a seller put these pages to use?
sections.html:
Pick the situation: an inherited house, a tenant in place, taxes behind, or a loan in foreclosure. Read the matching state guide, then find the county offices that carry it out.

When a deadline is involved, ask the office named in the statute for the exact day. The appraiser confirms exemption dates, the tax collector confirms balances, and the clerk confirms recording costs and sale dates. For a particular case, consult a Florida attorney.

Charter status also varies, since the Constitution recognizes both charter and non charter counties. If a city and county both claim a role in a permit or fee, the clerk's or appraiser's front desk can usually say which one bills you.

faqs.q: How many counties are in Florida?
faqs.a: Sixty-seven. Each elects a sheriff, tax collector, property appraiser, supervisor of elections and circuit court clerk.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to apply for a Florida homestead exemption?
faqs.a: March 1 each year, on Form DR-501 filed with the county property appraiser, with the home made a permanent residence by January 1.

faqs.q: What does a Florida deed cost in documentary stamp tax?
faqs.a: 70 cents per $100 of consideration in most counties. Miami-Dade uses 60 cents per $100 plus a 45 cent surtax that does not reach a single family home transfer.

faqs.q: When do Florida property taxes turn delinquent?
faqs.a: On April 1. Tax certificates go on sale for the unpaid items by June 1, after bills arrive in November.

faqs.q: Does Florida have an estate tax?
faqs.a: No. A federal change ended the state tax for people who died after 2004, and the revenue agency says estates no longer file the old estate tax return forms.
